## Panoramic Views of the Falls from the Brazilian Side

In Iguazu National Park, the main walking route connects panoramic viewpoints with sections close to the waterfalls. The forest frames the water and makes its force even more impressive. This excursion focuses on the Brazilian side; visits to trails on the Argentine side are part of a different itinerary.

The trip is ideal for a first introduction to Iguazu and for anyone who wants to see the cascades in broad, sweeping views. Bring protection for your phone or camera and a lightweight raincoat: the spray is part of the experience. The exact timing and order of visits depend on the excursion itinerary and the park's visiting conditions.

This excursion introduces you to Rio's principal and most striking sights in just one day. Your guide will collect you from the hotel in the morning, and you will travel by bus towards the foot of Corcovado Mountain. Along the way, you will admire churches, monasteries, the city's main cathedral and buildings in the colonial style. The route passes through central Rio, with its imposing bank skyscrapers and well-preserved colonial buildings. The Candelária Church, built in 1775, is described as an exact copy of a cathedral in Rome. The São Bento Monastery displays some of the finest examples of Baroque architecture. The famous Lapa Arches were constructed in 1732 and used as an aqueduct to carry water from the Carioca River to the city centre. The Municipal Theatre was decorated by some of Europe's finest artists. November Square contains several of the city's most important monuments: the Imperial Palace, from whose balcony the abolition of slavery was announced, the Tiradentes Palace, a cathedral built in 1808 as a royal church, and a sixteenth-century Carmelite convent. Boticarío Square has buildings with mosaics and old façades surrounded by centuries-old trees. Particularly impressive is the Metropolitan Cathedral, with a capacity of 20,000 people.

## Christ the Redeemer and Sugarloaf Mountain

You approach the foot of Corcovado, one of the most striking features of the landscape around the entrance to Guanabara Bay. Here you board a train with small carriages that takes you uphill through the rainforest, past remarkable tropical trees. After a short and pleasant walk from the upper station, you arrive at the feet of the immense Christ the Redeemer statue atop Corcovado. At 700 metres above sea level stands this symbol of Rio. From Corcovado, breathtaking panoramic views open across the city and its surroundings, including the Botanical Garden, Maracanã Stadium and Sugarloaf Mountain. The whole of Rio de Janeiro spreads out before you. There is time to enjoy the panorama of Rio and Guanabara Bay and take memorable photographs. You then descend on the same little train and travel to Praia Vermelha (Red Beach). From here, the cable car takes you up to the summit of Urca Mountain, which offers another extraordinary view of Rio. A second cable car carries you onwards to Sugarloaf Mountain (Pão de Açúcar). Its unusual shape is said to resemble a loaf of sugar, giving rise to its name. Another version derives the name from Pau-nh-acuqua, a word in the local Indigenous language meaning "High Hill". From the summit, the entire city comes into view, nestled between the mountains and the sea, while the rays of the sun setting beyond Copacabana Beach colour it with extraordinary shades. After descending by cable car, you will have lunch at one of the finest restaurants, then return to your hotel with your guide.

## The Charm of Villa de Leyva

The small town of Villa de Leyva invites you to discover the charm of colonial architecture. Built in the Spanish colonial style, with beautiful balconies, arches and inner courtyards, it has inspired poets, writers and artists. Sitting in the main square and breathing in the pure mountain air, you can immerse yourself in the colonial era and feel part of its history.

Villa de Leyva has been declared a national heritage site. Today it is one of the country's most important tourist centres. The town is full of welcoming restaurants in historic patios, museums and hotels. During the excursion you will also see the historic Boyacá Bridge.

Fossils are abundant here: even building façades and street paving contain astonishing numbers of ammonites. You may also see the fossilised remains of a marine dinosaur, Kronosaurus, described as the only one of its kind in South America and as having lived 20 million years ago.

## Panama: Three Cities in One

Panama City, founded by conquistadors in the sixteenth century, was the first Spanish port on the Pacific coast, used to ship gold, silver, pearls and other valuables taken from the Incas to Europe.

Today, Panama City is three cities in one: Panamá Viejo, or Old Panama; the colonial quarter of Casco Antiguo; and modern New Panama. Old Panama is full of seventeenth-century ruins: the cathedral, monasteries, bridges, the first hospital and the homes of the nobility.

## Casco Antiguo

Many colonial-era structures survive in Casco Antiguo. This part of the city has been declared a World Heritage Site and is protected by UNESCO. Its narrow cobbled streets, squares and parks preserve much of the country's history, despite successive waves of renewal and reconstruction.

Here stands the Presidential Palace, more than three centuries old. It is also known as the Palace of the Herons, or Palacio de las Garzas: in 1922 the president of the republic was given a pair of snow-white herons. He ordered them to be housed in the Moorish courtyard, where successive generations have wandered for decades. Near the Presidential Palace, in Cathedral Square, stands a magnificent cathedral with two towers inlaid with mother-of-pearl, sparkling in the bright tropical sun.

During the excursion we will visit the National Theatre, one of Panama's finest examples of Neoclassical architecture. We will walk through Plaza de Francia, visit San José Church and learn how its remarkable Golden Altar was saved from the pirates of Henry Morgan. A monument to Simón Bolívar, a national hero of many Central and South American countries, stands in Plaza Bolívar.

Las Bóvedas fortress was built in 1688 to protect the city from pirate attacks. Centuries later it was used as a military prison. Today Las Bóvedas houses an art gallery, a French restaurant and souvenir shops.

## Ancon Hill and the Causeway

Next we climb Ancon Hill to a viewpoint overlooking the Panama Canal and the city. Then we continue to the Causeway, one of Panama City's most remarkable areas. It was once three separate islands in the ocean: Naos, Perico and Flamenco. They were joined using rock excavated from the mountains during construction of the Panama Canal. A road leads along the Causeway with the vast Pacific Ocean on both sides. The islands offer excellent views of the city.

## New Panama and the Panama Canal

New Panama is an impressive modern city. Panama City's skyscrapers are the tallest in the region. Panama is growing before your eyes: it is described as the world's second-largest offshore zone after Hong Kong and the third-largest banking centre by assets.

During the tour we will also visit Miraflores Locks and watch ships pass through them. At the Miraflores Visitor Centre, we will enter the small Panama Canal museum to learn about this enormous twentieth-century engineering project, dubbed the "Eighth Wonder of the World". Visitors will also see a film about the canal's construction and operation.

We will drive through the residential former Canal Zone, where the Americans involved in building and operating the canal once lived, and along one of the capital's loveliest streets, Balboa Avenue, which follows the shore of Panama Bay.

During the excursion, your guide will recommend a restaurant for lunch according to your culinary tastes.

## Price

The price is $188. The excursion operates for groups of at least 2 people.

Búzios lies 177 km north of Rio de Janeiro. The group excursion lasts 12 hours, of which approximately 6 hours are spent on the return transfers. Búzios is a fishing village. Its distinctive charm comes from its unusual landscape, exotic vegetation and picturesque beaches. The climate is dry and temperate. Average temperatures: maximum 30 degrees, minimum 20.

## Full-Day Group Excursion to Búzios

Búzios delights visitors with its beaches of warm yellow sand and clear ocean water. The beaches offer beautiful views of forested mountains and coastal cliffs, while the sunsets here are especially colourful.

There are plenty of opportunities for diving, surfing, water-skiing and kayaking. You can hire a buggy and drive both along the beaches and around the town. Búzios has several viewpoints with magnificent vistas of the ocean and mountains.

On sailing-boat outings, you can enjoy wonderful views of the entire coastline and try a local drink, caipirinha. The boats stop out at sea, where you can swim and discover the colourful underwater world.

In the evening, cosy restaurants serving a wide variety of cuisines and nightclubs await you. The main pedestrian street comes alive after sunset. You can simply stroll, browse the shops or sit in one of the many bars and restaurants.

After the outing, return to the hotel.

## Duration and Price

12 hours including transfers. The round trip from Rio takes approximately 6 hours. The group excursion costs $104.
